answer:
GPT-3.5-Turbo (16K) gets about **45–46% accuracy** when the key is at the 200th of 300 positions. That is its lowest point in the 300-pair setting.

- **Where the value comes from:** The number is only drawn in Figure 7 on page 7 (right panel, "300 Key-Value Pairs (~16K tokens)"); the text never states it. I read it off the PDF page image. GPT-3.5-Turbo (16K) is the brown dashed line in the legend ("gpt-3.5-turbo-16k-0613"). At 200th its point lies just under halfway between the 40 and 50 gridlines. Since this is an estimate from the plot, treat it as roughly 45%, not an exact figure.
- **The rest of that curve (also estimated from the figure, p. 7):** about 100% at the 1st position, about 98% at 50th, about 95% at 100th and about 70% at 150th. It then climbs back to about 74% at 250th and about 100% at the 300th (last) position. That U-shape is what the paper calls "lost in the middle."
- **The paper's own description (p. 6):** "GPT-3.5-Turbo, GPT-3.5-Turbo (16K), and MPT-30B-Instruct have the lowest performance when they must access key-value pairs in the middle of their input context." The task setup is on p. 6: 75, 140 and 300 key-value pairs, 500 examples each.
- **For comparison (p. 7):** Claude-1.3 (100K), the orange line, stays near 99–100% at every position with 300 pairs.
